structural_counts.notes: n_models counts Table 1 (3), Table 2 (5) and S1 Table A3 (3). n_outcomes: entrepreneurial activity, nascent entrepreneurship, Plan-B motivation, business size, high-growth aspirations, new product, new technology. n_country_level_predictors counts distinct variables (3 work-family measures plus 6 controls; the paid-leave square is a term of the same variable). n_controls counts distinct control variables across models: age, age squared, postsecondary, 7 year dummies, sole owner, business age, not employed, 3 perception variables, plus the 6 country-level controls are listed under country-level predictors.

unusualness_reasoning: A standard cross-national multilevel design with random slopes and cross-level interactions; the only uncommon choices are the pooled nascent-plus-owner outcome, the 18-54 age window and the author-built leave series.

specificity.reason: Variables are defined in words with sources named, but survey-item codes, the labour-force operationalization, the 'established owner' operationalization, the imputation method for childcare, weighting, software and integration method are not given.

precision.reason: Coefficients and SEs are printed to two (sometimes three) decimals; tables carry several typographical problems (negative SE cell, blank cell, inconsistent AIC in the supplement) and no exact p values.

exhaustiveness.reason: The supplement reports three alternative specifications and descriptives, but many robustness checks are described only in footnotes without tables, the unconditional models for fn 17 are not shown, and the realized survey list is documented only in S1.

unavailable_source_fallbacks.item: FTE paid-leave weeks for mothers, annual 2001-2008
unavailable_source_fallbacks.fallback: Anchor on CEPR 2008 FTE values (21 countries); for the eight countries with policy changes (Denmark, Germany, Ireland, New Zealand, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom) back-cast pre-change values from OECD PF2.5 weeks and ILO payment rates; Czech Republic, Iceland and Poland from ILO 2009/2011 pages and PF2.5 weeks times legislated payment rate; apply the one-year lag.
unavailable_source_fallbacks.basis: MAIN p.12 fn 6-8; sources/leave_policy_documents.md; sources/oecd_sources.md PF2_5

unavailable_source_fallbacks.item: Childcare services spending (% GDP), 2012 Family Database vintage
unavailable_source_fallbacks.fallback: OECD PF3.1 time series (childcare plus pre-primary, current vintage) for every year; secondary alternative SOCX TP521 ECEC. Record as a vintage and definition change.
Current oecd_ftpt common-definition series; Japan employee series absent, use total employment for Japan.

unavailable_source_fallbacks.item: HDR GDP index by survey year
unavailable_source_fallbacks.fallback: Read the GDP index from HDR 2004-2009 tables and assign each report to survey year = report year minus two (HDR 2009 for 2007 and 2008); if any gap remains, compute the index from WDI GDP per capita PPP with the HDR formula.
unavailable_source_fallbacks.basis: sources/undp_worldbank_gem_sources.md (GDP index formula and reference-year note)
